accuracy.evidence: Statements were checked against Development Matters (2021) Literacy: birth to 3 'add some marks to their drawings, which they give meaning to, for example: That says mummy'; 3 to 4 'use some of their print and letter knowledge in their early writing, for example: writing a pretend shopping list that starts at the top of the page; writing m for mummy' and 'write some or all of their name'; and its five key concepts about print (print has meaning, print can have different purposes, we read English text from left to right and from top to bottom). The lab's list reads top down (milk, eggs, bread), the card reads left to right (To, Nana, love Mia), and Sam's name is S, A, M. Parameterised items (p1 lines = things, p2 3-n letters left, m6 x per kiss) validate at their corners.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented emergent-writing confusions: scribbles dismissed as meaningless (scene 1, p3, m7, challenge tag 'blank'); writing confused with drawing (sort scene refuses a picture in Writing, predict sun vs marks in a line, m1, tag 'pic'); not knowing print has different purposes (jobs scene refuses a card for the shop, p4, m2, m8, tag 'job'); reading bottom up or right to left (list and card refuse out-of-order taps, p5, m5, m9, tag 'dir'); and an unstable meaning that changes each reading (next-day choice, predict, m4, tag 'same').

lab_distinct.evidence: flagscribble is built round mark-making itself: free finger drawing that is stored as strokes on a paper and then given a meaning, a picture-versus-writing sort, a list/card/label/sign purpose match, building a name from its letters in order, and reading the child's own marks back in print order. It is not flagmarks, flagrefrain or flagnewword; the lab_distinct gate measured it under 30% overlap with every other flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers each idea by doing: a meaning cannot be chosen until marks are on the paper, and the label then reads 'Your marks say: a card for Nana'; sorting shows writing cards are small marks in a line; a sign dropped on the shop is refused with 'A sign is for the bedroom door'; tapping the bottom line first is refused ('Start at the top'). The completion text then names the rule in one sentence.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions, each with a tempting wrong option: 'Which one is writing?' (A big round sun vs Little marks in a line, disproved by the sort); 'Sam puts an S on his picture. What could it say?' (Nothing, it is just a line vs Sam, disproved when S, A, M spells his name); 'Mia reads her list again the next day. Does it say the same?' (No, marks change vs Yes, disproved by the next-day check where cake, cake, cake is refused).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions with rotating answer order; each wrong answer has its own message: 'blank' (marks can mean something, even scribbles), 'pic' (that is a picture; writing is small marks in a line), 'job' (each paper has its own job), 'dir' (start at the top of a list and on the left of a line), 'same' (marks keep their meaning), 'name' (S is the first letter of Sam and stands for his name).

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs use one idea per short sentence and everyday words (crayon, wiggles, shopping list); the validator holds kid text within grade 6.5 and adult text within 9.5. Lab prompts are one short instruction, on-canvas labels are single words (Card, List, Sign, Picture, Writing), and spoken feedback names the slip plainly.

no_filler.evidence: Each kid paragraph adds one concept (marks, meaning, writing versus pictures, reading order and stable meaning); the adult text gives the curriculum statements, how to model writing for real purposes, the named mistakes, and the lab outline. The content gate found no filler phrases and under 12% overlap with other lessons.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px screenshots in light and dark at the start, mid-way and end of each scene: the drawing paper fills most of the canvas width for finger strokes, meaning tiles show a large emoji and one bold word, cards and papers sit in 3 or 2 columns with text fitted to the card width (mini cards in the bins no longer overflow), letter tiles are about 100 px wide, and every scene has full-width buttons below.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button: Make marks plus three It says buttons, card → Picture/Writing, paper → place, each letter, Read line N, Read mark N and the next-day answers. Each action updates the canvas aria-label and the c.say live region. walk.cjs ran axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13 with no violations; canvas text is dark ink on white or tinted paper.
